description.narrative:
Projektet förväntas bidra till följande övergripande mål: mobilitet och demografisk övergång blir vektorer för positiv förändring och välstånd för alla människor, bidra till en inkluderande och hållbar utveckling.
Projektet syftar till att leverera en trefaldig förändring som kommer att främjas av insatser som syftar till att främja cirkulär migration: 1) En växande relation av ömsesidig förståelse, tillit och samarbete mellan det serbiska samhället och den serbiska diasporan, som är baserad på hållbara lösningar (t.ex. som: policy- och regleringsinitiativ föreslagna av returpunkten till relevanta institutioner, inrättandet av Carta Serbica-programmet, diasporalåneprogrammet), 2) Ett växande intresse för att knyta an till Serbien bland den serbiska diasporan, vilket framgår av engagemang i landets ekonomiska, sociala och kulturella liv, och av en växande Returning Point-gemenskap. 3) En stödjande miljö för utländska skickliga yrkesverksamma att välja att komma, bo och arbeta i Serbien, driven av ett förbättrat rättsligt ramverk och serviceleveransdrivet nätverk inom administrationen.

The project is expected to contribute to the following overarching goal: mobility and demographic transition become vectors for positive change and prosperity for all people, contributing to inclusive and sustainable development.
The project aims to deliver a threefold change that will be fostered by interventions aimed at promoting circular migration: 1) A growing relationship of mutual understanding, trust and cooperation between the Serbian society and the Serbian diaspora, which is based on the sustainable solutions (such as: policy and regulatory initiatives proposed by the Returning Point to the relevant institutions, the establishment of the Carta Serbica program, the diaspora loan scheme), 2) A growing interest in connecting with Serbia among the Serbian diaspora, as evidenced by engagement in the country’s economic, social, and cultural life, and by a growing Returning Point community. 3) A supportive environment for foreign skilled professionals to choose to come, live and work in Serbia, propelled by an improved legal framework and service­delivery driven network within the administration.

The project is expected to achieve the following outcomes: 1) Establishment of the Returning Point Platform 2) Channeling diaspora based businesses, trade and circular migration initiatives for sustainable local development 3) Developing model for diaspora Investments 4) Developing and improving diaspora and circular migration services 5) Improved Support Services for Foreigners to Relocate to Serbia

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
Progress of the project in its second year of implementation can be summarized in the following way:
- Model for Bilateral Social Security Agreements developed and submitted to the Ministry of Labour, Employment, Veteran and Social Policy for review. This represents a major milestone in creating a more predictable and fair social protection framework, addressing a long-standing structural barrier for circular migrants and returnees at the national level.
- A practical guide for Migration Service Center (MSC) employees was developed, equipping them with actionable tools and methodologies to strengthen local-level support for returnees.
- Over 2,800 Serbian researchers were mapped at the worlds top 300 universities, creating an evidence base for scientific diaspora engagement and knowledge circulation.
- FThe project unlocked new momentum through cooperation and exchange with partners in South East European (SEE) countries, proving to be mutually beneficial as obstacles and solutions can be the same or similar.
- Regional brainstorming session on circular migration organized in Belgrade, bringing together partners from five countries and laying the groundwork for the 2026 Regional Circular Migration Forum.
- 'Umreene' initiative for women entrepreneurs strengthened through continued mentoring, practical support, and community-building, building on the network established in 2024.
- The "Umreene" initiative successfully hosted a workshop for 24 women entrepreneurs (15 new, 9 returning) and expanding its network with 5 new mentors. This result confirms the model's effectiveness in building a durable, gender-responsive support system for business growth.
- The "RP Café" format was successfully piloted in five European cities (Vienna, Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Prague, Zurich), establishing a new, trust-based model for direct dialogue with diaspora communities abroad.
- Four Serbian Expat Meetups organized, with over 400 attendees, fostering peer-to-peer relationships that are not just social but catalytic, and evolving from networking events into a platform for collective action.
- The Serbian Expat Community successfully mobilized funds for a donation campaign to renovate a terrace at the University Childrens Hospital, demonstrating the communitys readiness to engage in tangible local development initiatives.
- Returning Points communications platform expanded significantly, publishing 15 new podcast episodes (including the 100th episode milestone) and reaching over 584,000 YouTube viewers and 1.95 million social media views.
